chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn Al-Numan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The boundary of Al-Muzdalifa is from Muhassar up to the two narrow points.

key_terms.الْمَأْزِمَيْنِ: The two narrow points, referring to specific geographical constraints or landmarks marking the end of the Muzdalifa boundary.
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifa, the plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the night after leaving Arafat.
key_terms.مُحَسِّر: Muhassar, a specific location or landmark marking the starting point of the Muzdalifa boundary.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific boundaries of Al-Muzdalifa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi precisely delineates the geographical boundaries of Al-Muzdalifa, extending from Muhassar to Al-Ma'ziman, which is essential for determining the validity of the 'standing' (wuquf) ritual. In Shia jurisprudence, this specific definition clarifies the spatial limits for pilgrims during the night of Arafat, ensuring compliance with the prophetic tradition regarding the duration and location of the stay. The narration underscores the importance of precise geographical knowledge in fulfilling the ritual obligations of Hajj correctly.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A boundary of Al-Muzdalifa is from Muhassar up to the two narrow points’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from Ali ibn al-Nu’man ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan forms who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The boundaries of al-Muzdalifah are from Muhassar to al-Mazemin.’”
